summary: End-to-end frontend testing of Prop Firm Risk Matrix & Strategy Simulator mobile app. App loads cleanly on Dashboard with all 12 KPI cards, strategy-grade badge, and Control Panel FAB. Control Panel bottom sheet opens correctly and exposes all 21 input/control testIDs (account/strategy/simulation inputs, consistency chips, DD toggles, reset and run buttons). Changing Win Rate 50→60 and RR 2→2.5 propagates to Dashboard KPIs (Pass Probability 99.9%→100.0%, Profit Factor 2.00→3.75, grade stays A+). Matrices tab renders heatmap-matrix with cells heat-cell-0-0 through heat-cell-15-7; cell tap opens CellDetailModal which closes via cell-detail-close; seg-pass / seg-roi segment toggle changes cell values. Simulator empty state shows then transitions to equity-chart-card + drawdown chart + pass-prob/RoR stat boxes after run-from-simulator. Tools tab shows all 6 tool cards. Each pushed sub-route renders the expected content testIDs (analyzer rows, 3 optimizer reco cards, 6 account cards with recommended-badge, variance-high/low, recovery-chart + recovery-row-10..75, settings-reset). Settings reset successfully reverts inputs (Account 100000, WR 50, RR 2). ISSUES FOUND: (1) back-button testID is MISSING on 5 of 6 sub-routes (optimizer, settings, account-comparison, variance, drawdown-recovery) — only strategy-analyzer.tsx has it. The Pressable + chevron-back UI element exists on every screen but lacks the testID. (2) Strategy Optimizer returns IDENTICAL metrics for Safe, Balanced and Aggressive recommendations (all three show Risk 0.25% / RR 3.00 / Pass 100% / ROI 1500% / RoR 0.0% / DD 2% / Position $250) — the ranking algorithm collapses when pass probability saturates at 100% across most candidates. (3) Default-input Pass Probability (50% WR, 2 RR, 1% risk, 10% target, 10% maxDD) yields 99.9% which feels unrealistically optimistic and may indicate the closed-form pass formula does not adequately penalise drawdown risk. No crashes, no red screens, no deprecated Expo packages (expo-av/barcode/background-fetch). Console warnings: "shadow*" and "props.pointerEvents" RN-web deprecations (cosmetic). The tab bar items render as <a role="tab"> in expo-router web and the configured tabBarTestID is not propagated to the DOM (known expo-router web limitation), so tab-dashboard/tab-matrices/tab-simulator/tab-tools testIDs are not selectable on web preview — text/role selector used as workaround.

integration_issues.issue: Safe / Balanced / Aggressive cards all show identical metrics for default inputs (Risk 0.25%, RR 3.00, Pass 100%, ROI 1500%, RoR 0%, DD 2%, Position $250). Root cause: in optimizer.tsx useMemo, when passProbabilityClosedForm saturates to 100% across many (risk, rr) candidates the sort criteria collapse — safe sorts by pass DESC (100 ties → first), balanced and aggressive both sort by roi DESC and since pass=100 and fee is constant ROI is identical across many candidates → all three converge to the same first row. Need differentiated ranking (e.g., safe: lowest risk among ror<=0.05; balanced: ror<=0.15 AND best Sharpe-like metric; aggressive: highest risk among grade>=B) so the three cards actually differ.

Defaults (50% WR, 2 RR, 1% risk/trade, 10% target, 10% maxDD) produce 99.9% pass probability — appears overly optimistic. Verify passProbabilityClosedForm correctly models barrier-hitting (target hit before max DD hit) with finite trade horizon. Consider unit-checking against Monte Carlo at the same inputs.

issues: Console warnings: "shadow*" style props deprecated (use boxShadow), props.pointerEvents deprecated (use style.pointerEvents). Cosmetic on web but should be fixed for forward-compat with RN 0.76+.

rca_of_issue: Back-button testIDs: only strategy-analyzer.tsx received the testID prop during initial implementation; the same pattern was not propagated to optimizer/settings/account-comparison/variance/drawdown-recovery (grep confirms only 1 occurrence of "back-button" across /app/frontend/app/). Optimizer collapse: in optimizer.tsx the candidate list ranking relies on `pass` (safe) and `roi` (balanced+aggressive). Both metrics saturate when pass=100% for many candidates because the closed-form pass probability is too optimistic; the stable sort then returns the same first row for all three profiles. Fix requires both (a) per-profile criteria differentiation (e.g., aggressive = highest risk with grade>=B; balanced = best Sharpe-like score; safe = lowest risk meeting ror<=0.05) and ideally (b) tightening passProbabilityClosedForm so it doesn't saturate so easily.
